newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: BPI says Victorias loans not worrisome.
newsitem.headline: BPI says Victorias loans not worrisome.

text.p: The Bank of the Philippine Islands said on Tuesday its net income in the first two months of 1997 were close to one billion pesos and its loans to Victorias Milling Co should not cause concern.

BPI President Xavier Loinaz, who gave the two-month profit figure and also sought to allay fears over the bank's loans to the financially troubled Victorias Milling Co, told a stockholders meeting the bank's total exposure to Victorias was at 700 million pesos.
Victorias Milling, the country's biggest sugar miller, last week reported problems in repaying debts worth 4.423 billion pesos ($168 million) to 32 banks.
It sought a 90-day moratorium on principal repayments.
Loinaz said of BPI's total exposure of 700 million pesos to the Victorias group, 450 million was to the parent company which has debt problems.
Victorias' subsidiaries have not had debt difficulties.
Loinaz noted that the 450 million pesos exposure represents just one-half of one percent of total loans in BPI and is two percent of BPI's capital.

He said the bulk of the loans are covered by collateral on equipment and plants. He said the problem with Victorias is not one of insolvency but a temporary liquidity problem caused by market conditions.
"At the end of the day, with some degree of restructuring...a solution will be found," he said.

The bank reported an audited net income of 4.013 billion pesos in 1996 compared with 2.946 billion pesos in 1995. The 1995 figure includes earnings from CityTrust Banking Corp, with which BPI merged. ($1=26.30 pesos)
